    Strong pairwise inference for Dune management groups

    dune-strong-pairwise.Rmd

    Why this is a separate engine

    A single permutation distribution formed by mixing every management group is valid under the complete null, but it is not invariant under a partial null such as BF = HF when NM and SF really differ. Strong familywise control therefore needs a separate valid action for every intersection hypothesis.

    permanova_pairwise_strong() constructs the graph of equalities in each intersection. Observations are reassigned only inside its connected equality components, with original group sizes preserved; all other groups stay fixed. The maximum pairwise pseudo-F tests that intersection. Closed testing then takes the largest p-value over every intersection containing a pair.

    This proof is deliberately narrower than a generic PERMANOVA location claim. It assumes independent observations and equality of the complete observation distributions within each true-null component. Equal centroids with unequal dispersion or shape do not provide the required exchangeability.

    Bray–Curtis analysis 

    library(distmer)
data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")

design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management,
  dune.env,
  vegan::vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
)

fit <- permanova_pairwise_strong(
  design,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260726
)

fit$table[, c("contrast", "pseudo_f", "p_perm", "p_closed")]
#>         contrast  pseudo_f     p_perm  p_closed
#> BF - HF  BF - HF 0.9141421 0.19642857 0.1964286
#> BF - NM  BF - NM 3.2009023 0.02380952 0.0550000
#> BF - SF  BF - SF 2.2705377 0.05952381 0.0750000
#> HF - NM  HF - NM 3.6817517 0.02500000 0.0450000
#> HF - SF  HF - SF 1.5990807 0.13000000 0.1850000
#> NM - SF  NM - SF 4.2824464 0.00500000 0.0250000

    The unadjusted p_perm column comes from the singleton intersection for that pair. p_closed is the strong-FWER adjusted value. Sixty-three intersections are required for the six pairwise hypotheses among four management levels.

    fit$permutation
#> $algorithm
#> [1] "intersection-specific component label reassignment"
#> 
#> $intersections
#> [1] 63
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 20260726
#> 
#> $exact
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $maximum_attainable
#> [1] 6518191680
#> 
#> $total_used
#> [1] 12164
fit$exchangeability_proof
#> [1] "For every intersection S, the selected equality edges form connected components. Under equality of the complete observation distributions within each component, the joint data law is invariant to every sample-size-preserving raw-label reassignment used for S. Therefore the non-null groups outside those components remain fixed, and the intersection maximum-F permutation test is level alpha. Closed testing rejects an elementary pair only when every containing intersection is rejected, giving strong FWER control without a subset-pivotality claim."
head(fit$intersections[, c(
  "intersection", "components", "p_perm", "attainable", "used"
)])
#>   intersection components     p_perm attainable used
#> 1      BF - HF    BF = HF 0.19642857         56   56
#> 2      BF - NM    BF = NM 0.02380952         84   84
#> 3      BF - SF    BF = SF 0.05952381         84   84
#> 4      HF - NM    HF = NM 0.02500000        462  199
#> 5      HF - SF    HF = SF 0.13000000        462  199
#> 6      NM - SF    NM = SF 0.00500000        924  199

    The attainable space differs by intersection because only levels joined by the asserted equalities may exchange observations. Monte Carlo p-values use a plus-one correction. Requesting permutations = "all" is allowed only when every unique label-assignment space is below max_exact.

    What this result does not say

    The test statistic is centroid-sensitive, but the finite-sample permutation null is equality of complete distributions. A significant pair can reflect location, dispersion, shape, or a combination. Use a design-aware dispersion analysis and ecological diagnostics to interpret that distinction. Planned non-pairwise contrasts, dependent observations, repeated measures, and mixed designs are not routed through this engine because their subset-null exchangeability groups have not been proved.
